newsitem.title: USA: US bus group urges House to keep diesel tax break.
newsitem.headline: US bus group urges House to keep diesel tax break.

text.p: The American Bus Association Wednesday urged House lawmakers not to repeal a 17 cents tax credit which intercity buses receive on the diesel tax of 24.3 cents per gallon, in a letter released Wednesday.

"We believe that Congress should consider restoring full intercity bus (tax) exemption or, at the very least, preserve the existing partial exemption," said Peter Pantuso, president and CEO of the association.

In letters sent last week to members of the House Ways and Means Committee, which is about to review transportation excise taxes, the group said federal subsidies to other modes of transport had made intercity bus service less competitive.

A 1995 study that "the market for passenger transportation has been seriously distorted in that relative lack of support for intercity bus service has been a major contributing force to the decline of bus service," the November 18 letters said.
The bus group said the tax break should be continued in order to help passengers, who "are largely those who cannot afford ... other modes of transportation."

The group said intercity buses should be allowed to buy diesel tax free, just as publicly-owned bus fleets did. It added that a total tax exemption for buses would save the government the administrative costs of refunding a tax credit.
